correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact level-2 aging theorem and white-region lemma of Edelsbrunner--Garber--Saghafian, an arbitrary COMPLETE level-2 hypertriangulation H has a unique complete ordinary underlying triangulation P. Every black hypertriangle is a medial triangle and every white hypertriangle rooted at x a 1/2 homothetic image of its original-scale triangle. For each x the white triangles plus old triangles not incident to x form a complete triangulation P^{-x} of A\{x}, including when x is a hull vertex because the white region intersects conv(A\{x}). Hence 2c(H)=max(c(P), max_x c(P^{-x})); the result is independent of non-Delaunay triangulations. For Del_2(A), black triangles correspond to Del(A); each white triangle is the replacement of the single Delaunay triangle after deleting x, so P^{-x}=Del(A\{x}) by the empty-circle criterion and generic no-four-cocircular assumption. Rajan's ordinary min-containment theorem separately bounds each component against its Delaunay counterpart. Thus the global inequality follows. The proof explicitly uses SMALLest enclosing circles, not circumcircles; it does not presume all hypertriangles acute.

originality.rationale: The primary Edelsbrunner--Garber--Saghafian paper establishes order-two angle optimality and asks in its conclusion whether the smallest-enclosing-circle property generalizes. Rajan's 1994 theorem only handles ordinary triangulations. The new exact decomposition into P and all one-point deletions is necessary to transfer the ordinary theorem to the constrained level-two competitors. A mere parameter substitution in Rajan cannot establish it.
residual_risks: The central aging and white-region lemma is imported from original paper rather than formally re-proved; all complete-competitor hypotheses must be retained.
The theorem is not uniqueness and does not cover incomplete hypertriangulations or levels k>=3; subtle degeneracies ruled out by no-three-collinear/no-four-cocircular.
Potential alternate undocumented proof of the explicit open question; novelty search nonexhaustive.
